Unlike scalar functions, for which all zeros and poles are characterized solely by their orders, operator-valued functions exhibit a more intricate structure: zeros are characterized by finite-dimensional spaces of vector functions, called root functions, whereas poles are characterized by finite-dimensional spaces of pole cancellation functions. For this purpose, we use the following definitions of a root function and related concepts, which are consistent with the corresponding definitions in [1,3,5,7].
